note: Three Linux File::create sites directly establish the disclosed transient-readable-permissions defect. The patch also hardens stream write permissions and std::fs::copy fallbacks on multiple platforms. Those changes alone do not prove all such sites independently expose private contents: historical standard-library creation semantics and the CVE scope of the write-permission variant need review. They are not promoted to vulnerable functions merely because the patch touched them.

Seven source-qualified content-copy locations are confirmed from the common no-dereference check/use sequence, including explicit stream opens on other Unix and macOS. The previous other.rs mapping is withdrawn: that is the non-Unix backend, not other_unix.rs, and the Linux O_NOFOLLOW evidence does not establish its native copy semantics. Exhaustive coverage still requires primary evidence for the non-Unix delegated copy and macOS clonefile/native fallback semantics. Probe-only opens are not automatically vulnerable locations.
Compile-time platform gates; no singular runtime function is established as the vulnerable unit.
